title.value: A debriefing tool to acquire non-technical skills in trauma courses
title.justification: The paper focuses on a debriefing tool designed to enhance non-technical skills in trauma courses. This is a key element of the study, as indicated by the title and throughout the abstract and discussion sections.
title.quote:
Objective: The study reports the use of a nominal group technique (NGT) to evaluate the PEARLS Healthcare
debriefing tool as a tool to foster non-technical skills in trauma simulation courses. Additionally, it introduces a
debriefing card to be used in trauma courses.

extractions.description: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of the PEARLS Healthcare debriefing tool for promoting non-technical skills in trauma simulation courses. Using a nominal group technique, experts assessed the tool's strategies, such as focused facilitation and self-assessment. The study culminates in the creation of a specific debriefing tool to be used in trauma scenarios, aiming to improve skills like communication and leadership in clinical settings. The research suggests that structured debriefing could enhance training efficiency and equitable learning, moving beyond traditional technical skills focus.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is centered on improving educational tools and strategies for acquiring non-technical skills in trauma courses. It does not directly address climate or ecologically-related sustainable development, although enhancing healthcare skills can have indirect societal benefits. The main focus is on educational methodologies rather than environmental impact or sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In conclusion, this nominal group study supports PEARLS strategies for non-technical skills training in trauma courses. The process resulted in a debriefing card to promote better debriefing in simulation courses, including different specialties.

primary_category.justification: The content of the paper does not focus on any aspect of climate or ecologically-related sustainable development, but rather on educational approaches in medical simulation training.
primary_category.quote:
We hypothesize that in complex trauma simulated scenarios teams who receive structured non-technical skills debriefing
perform better than those who only receive technical skills debriefing.

primary_sub_category.justification: The topic revolves around non-technical skills in medical education and does not fit into any of the specified sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainability.
primary_sub_category.quote: The PEARLS (Promoting Excellence and Reflective Learning in Simulation) Healthcare Debriefing Tool [5] has become accepted as a framework with the potential to promote non-technical skills.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper remains firmly within the realm of medical education and training, not touching upon new areas that would necessitate introducing a new category related to climate or ecological sustainability.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Given the content focused on medical education innovations, there is no indication of a need for a new sub-category specific to climate or ecological sustainability.
